source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: When a model must critique and revise its own answer with no outside signal, accuracy falls. Gains in earlier papers came from using the true label to decide when to stop.
numbers: GPT-3.5: GSM8K 75.9 -> 74.7 (5 calls), CommonSenseQA 75.8 -> 38.1 (3 calls) / 41.8 (5), HotpotQA 26.0 -> 25.0. GPT-4: GSM8K 95.5 -> 89.0, CSQA 82.0 -> 80.0, HotpotQA 49.0 -> 43.0 (100 items). With oracle label GPT-4 reaches 97.5 / 85.5 / 59.0.
limits: Two rounds max; several alternative critique prompts also lowered accuracy (their Tables 5-6). Table 2 was garbled in text extraction; oracle rows read by position.
agent_relevance: Direct support for G1 and G2. A red-team pass that runs by itself, with no failing output, harms. Doubt must be triggered by a real check.

source: Huang et al. (2024) flip analysis
finding: Most damage is correct answers turned wrong. On GSM8K GPT-3.5 leaves most answers unchanged; on CommonSenseQA it flips many because wrong options look plausible.
numbers: GPT-3.5 GSM8K: 74.7% of answers unchanged after correction. Correct->incorrect flips outweigh incorrect->correct on CommonSenseQA (read from a figure).
limits: Only the 74.7% figure read with confidence; others from a garbled figure.
agent_relevance: A challenge step is most dangerous on tasks with plausible distractors. Prefer a code check over a challenge prompt.

source: Huang et al. (2024) oracle-label caveat
finding: Earlier self-correction gains (Kim 2023, Shinn 2023) used ground-truth labels to stop. That is not self-correction.
numbers: Oracle rows: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 89.7 vs 75.8 baseline; GPT-4 HotpotQA 59.0 vs 49.0. Without oracle both fall.
limits: Original earlier papers not opened.
agent_relevance: When any paper claims a critique loop helped, check for a hidden oracle signal.

source: Tyen et al. (2024) LLMs cannot find reasoning errors, but can correct them given the error location
finding: Models are poor at finding where their own chain of thought went wrong but fix it well once told. Built BIG-Bench Mistake, 2186 step-labelled traces.
numbers: GPT-4 best, only 52.87 overall mistake-finding accuracy with direct step prompting; GPT-3.5-Turbo as low as 1.67 to 19 on some tasks. Backtracking with true location: multistep arithmetic +43.92 on wrong traces (-6.67 on right ones); with random location +20.39 (-6.67). Dyck +36.86 vs +21.57.
limits: Synthetic tasks (word sorting, Dyck, arithmetic). Traces 85% incorrect, 15% correct. A trained mistake classifier helps only above roughly 60 to 70% accuracy.
agent_relevance: Finding the flaw is the weak part of red teaming; repair is cheap. Supports G2: locate the error with code or test output, then let the model fix it.

source: Kamoi et al. (2024) When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? Critical Survey
finding: No prior work shows successful self-correction using feedback from a prompted model on general tasks. It works with reliable external feedback or after large-scale fine-tuning.
numbers: Four findings: none for prompted self-feedback in general tasks; works with code interpreters or web search; fine-tuning helps; a few tasks are exceptions. Papers up to May 2024.
limits: Survey, no new experiments.
agent_relevance: Boundary: LLM red teaming is useful only when critique is grounded in tools, tests or retrieved evidence.

source: Du et al. (2023) Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
finding: Several copies propose, read each other, revise. Beat single agent and self-reflection on arithmetic, math, chess, facts.
numbers: 3 agents, 2 rounds. Arithmetic: single 67.0, reflection 72.1, majority 69.0, debate 81.8. GSM8K 77.0 / 75.0 / 81.0 / 85.0. Biographies 66.0 / 68.3 / - / 73.8. MMLU 63.9 / 57.7 / - / 71.1. Chess validity 29.3 / 38.8 / - / 45.2. Mixed personas on MMLU 71.1 to 74.2.
limits: Mostly gpt-3.5. Later re-tests (c08, c10) do not reproduce the margin over strong baselines. Self-reflection hurt on MMLU here.
agent_relevance: Founding LLM analogue of a red-team cell. G4: copies of one model are not independent, so a hint, not proof.

source: Smit et al. (2024) Should we be going MAD?
finding: Compared debate strategies on seven datasets (MedQA, PubMedQA, MMLU, CosmosQA, CIAR, GPQA, Chess). Debate did not consistently beat cheaper non-debate prompting.
numbers: Best MedQA debate setups about 61%. Medprompt (no debate) best overall and cheaper; Multi-Persona about 7% worse than Medprompt. Single-agent and self-consistency results swung a lot with prompt wording.
limits: Debate very sensitive to hyperparameters.
agent_relevance: Do not assume an adversarial stage pays for its cost. Compare to self-consistency at equal compute.

source: Liang et al. (2024) Encouraging Divergent Thinking in LLMs through Multi-Agent Debate
finding: Self-reflection suffers 'degeneration of thought': once confident the model will not produce new views. Adding an opposing debater plus judge fixed part of it.
numbers: Counter-Intuitive Arithmetic (200 Qs): GPT-3.5-Turbo 26.0, +CoT 28.0, +self-consistency 29.5, +self-reflect 27.5, +MAD 37.0; GPT-4 alone 51.0. Translation judge scores 79.9 to 84.4 by debater/judge model.
limits: Modest gains, small sets, same-model debaters share biases.
agent_relevance: A separate opposing role beats same-model self-reflection, but 37.0 still trails GPT-4 at 51.0.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Rethinking the Bounds of LLM Reasoning: Are Multi-Agent Discussions the Key?
finding: A single agent with a strong prompt (one demonstration or full question description) nearly matches the best discussion framework. Discussion wins only when the prompt has no demonstration.
numbers: Tested on FOLIO-wiki and other sets across backbones; per-task numbers not extracted. Stronger LLMs in mixed discussions help weaker ones.
limits: Qualitative only here.
agent_relevance: A strong single prompt may replace a red-team agent. Test that arm first.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Stop Overvaluing Multi-Agent Debate
finding: Five debate frameworks, 9 benchmarks, 4 models: debate often fails to beat chain-of-thought and self-consistency despite far more compute. Mixing different models helps.
numbers: GPT-4o-mini: Society of Mind below CoT on all 9 sets; ChatEval and AgentVerse beat CoT on 1 of 9. Claude-3.5-haiku MMLU: only AgentVerse beats CoT (+0.85); others at least 3.60 lower. AgentVerse beats CoT in about 15% of cases. Self-consistency generally best.
limits: Heterogeneity explored, not designed.
agent_relevance: Strongest recent counter to adding a debate red team. Use a different model as adversary (G4) and compare to self-consistency.

source: Wynn, Satija, Hadfield (2025) Talk Isn't Always Cheap
finding: Debate can lower accuracy over rounds. Agents flip correct to incorrect more than the reverse, driven by peer agreement, even when strong models outnumber weak.
numbers: GPT-4o-mini, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B on CommonSenseQA, MMLU, GSM8K. Correct->incorrect flips exceed incorrect->correct in later rounds; resistance drops after round 2; flip rate tied to number of disagreeing peers.
limits: Small models; percentages are in figures, not recorded.
agent_relevance: Conformity defeats a devil's advocate. The adversary must not talk the main reasoner out of a verified answer.

source: Sharma et al. (2024) Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
finding: Assistants give in when challenged even when first right; user belief biases answers; preference models reward agreement.
numbers: Claude 1.3 wrongly admits mistakes on 98% of questions. A user suggesting a wrong answer lowers accuracy by up to 27% (LLaMA 2).
limits: Older assistants; newer ones are trained against some of this.
agent_relevance: A bare 'are you sure' challenge makes the model fold. The red-team stage must show evidence.

source: Dhuliawala et al. (2024) Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination
finding: Built-in challenge loop: draft, plan verification questions, answer them independently, revise. Independent (factored) verification beat joint.
numbers: Llama 65B Wikidata list precision: few-shot 0.17, CoVe joint 0.29, two-step 0.36, factored 0.32. FACTSCORE: few-shot 55.9, joint 60.8, factored 63.7, factor+revise 71.4; ChatGPT 58.7; PerplexityAI 61.6.
limits: Fact tasks; verifier is the same model, no tool.
agent_relevance: Working example of red-teaming a draft inside an LLM loop. Independence matters: verifier must not see the draft (G5).

source: Gou et al. (2024) CRITIC: LLMs Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing
finding: Critique that calls tools (search, code, calculator) improves output; the same loop without tools gives much less.
numbers: One block of Table 1 (EM/F1 on AmbigNQ, TriviaQA, HotpotQA): CRITIC 50.0/64.9, 72.7/80.6, 38.7/50.5 vs CRITIC w/o Tool 42.0/58.3, 67.3/74.7, 34.9/46.1; another block CRITIC 59.8/71.8, 77.0/83.7, 43.1/54.5.
limits: Backbone for each block not confirmed; read as tool vs no-tool contrast.
agent_relevance: Matches G2. The challenger runs a check, not an opinion.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Devil's Advocate: Anticipatory Reflection for LLM Agents
finding: Agent loop that before each action asks what could go wrong and prepares a backup, then checks results and revises the plan. A pre-mortem inside an agent.
numbers: WebArena success 23.5% after seven episodes vs LATS 22.7% and Plan+Act 19.8%; +3.5 points over zero-shot baselines; 45% fewer plan revisions.
limits: About 1 point over LATS; one benchmark; GPT-4 based; agent still often fails to learn from past failure.
agent_relevance: Closest direct use of red-team doubt in an agent loop. It fires before every action (a schedule), so G1 says test it.

source: Lee et al. (2025) Conversational Agents as Catalysts for Critical Thinking (LLM devil's advocate)
finding: Human test of an LLM devil's advocate in four-person groups with one junior. Satisfaction rose, workload rose slightly, psychological safety not clearly changed.
numbers: 48 participants, 12 groups (3 senior, 1 junior), baseline vs AI within group. Process and outcome satisfaction significantly higher; juniors' safety rise not significant; load up slightly, not significant. Seniors said usefulness faded.
limits: Tiny sample, CHI extended abstract, no decision-quality measure.
agent_relevance: Satisfaction is not accuracy. No evidence here that a devil's advocate improves the decision.

source: Alsobay, Rothschild, Hofman, Goldstein (2026) Bringing Everyone to the Table
finding: Large preregistered test of GPT-4o as group facilitator. It raised information shared but did not change the final decision.
numbers: 1,475 participants, 281 groups, four conditions (none, one-time message, human, GPT-4o). Information sharing up by lifting least-engaged members; no significant effect on decision outcome in a hidden-profile task.
limits: Facilitation, not adversarial challenge.
agent_relevance: Richer discussion need not improve the answer; judge by outcome.

source: Perez et al. (2022) Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models
finding: One LM generates test cases to find failures of a 280B chatbot. RL gave most failures but narrow ones.
numbers: 0.5M zero-shot cases: offensive replies 3.7% (18,444 failures). RL with low KL penalty: over 40% offensive; 78% of those cases contained the word 'invisible'.
limits: Safety red teaming, not analytic. Needs an offensiveness classifier as grader.
agent_relevance: An automatic adversary works when a classifier supplies ground truth; diversity collapses without a penalty.

source: Lamparth et al. (2024) Human vs. Machine: Expert Humans and LMs in Wargame Simulations
finding: 214 national-security experts versus LLM-simulated teams in a US-China crisis wargame. High-level agreement but LLMs more aggressive, scenario-sensitive; simulated dialogue is farcically harmonious.
numbers: 214 experts; 80 simulated games per treatment combination. Personas such as 'pacifist' or 'aggressive sociopath' gave no significant difference.
limits: One fictional scenario; 2023-24 models.
agent_relevance: LLM red-team teams will not give real dissent; persona prompts barely move behavior. Persona voters are not independent (G4).

source: Rivera et al. (2024) Escalation Risks from Language Models in Military and Diplomatic Decision-Making
finding: Eight nation agents using the same model in a simulated wargame. All five off-the-shelf LLMs showed escalation and arms-race dynamics.
numbers: Five LLMs; escalation rises over time in all models and scenarios under the authors' scoring.
limits: Authors' own simulator and score; exact figures not recorded.
agent_relevance: Same-model agents reinforce each other; a same-model red team does not break this.

source: Lee et al. (2025) Amplifying Minority Voices: AI-Mediated Devil's Advocate System
finding: Design paper for an LLM that restates minority opinions as its own to protect anonymity. Seen only in a search snippet.
numbers: No numbers read.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Low priority; do not cite numbers.

source: Synthesis across Perez 2022, Gou 2024, Kamoi 2024: grader requirement
finding: Adversary success depends on an external grader (classifier, tool, test), not on the adversary's own judgment.
numbers: Perez: classifier-graded failures. CRITIC: tool vs no-tool gap about 5 to 8 EM points. Kamoi: no case of prompted self-feedback working in general tasks.
limits: Synthesis of opened sources, not new data.
agent_relevance: Pair every adversary with a code or tool grader.

source: Zhang 2025 with Wynn 2025: model heterogeneity
finding: Mixing models from different families helped debate consistently, yet a weak model can drag a strong one down.
numbers: Zhang: heterogeneity improved MAD frameworks. Wynn: weaker agents added to stronger ones can reduce accuracy.
limits: Sources differ with the strength gap.
agent_relevance: If several models are available, use a different, matched-strength model as challenger.

source: Tyen 2024 with Huang 2024: locating versus fixing
finding: Asking a model whether it is wrong hurts; telling it where it is wrong helps.
numbers: Huang GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 -> 89.0 with self-critique; Tyen true-location backtracking +43.92 on wrong arithmetic traces.
limits: Different tasks and models; indicative only.
agent_relevance: Locator in code (tests, constraint checks); repairer is the model.

source: Liang 2024 versus Zhang 2025: do debate gains replicate
finding: Earlier debate gains were measured against weak baselines; the 2025 re-test with stronger baselines finds little or no gain.
numbers: Liang: 26.0 -> 37.0. Zhang: Society of Mind below CoT on 9 of 9 sets (GPT-4o-mini); ChatEval and AgentVerse above on 1 of 9.
limits: Different tasks; not a direct replication.
agent_relevance: Treat debate gains as unproven against self-consistency.
